leadText:
A Picnicker (Japanese: ピクニックガール Picnic Girl) is a type of Pokémon Trainer that first debuted in the Generation I games. They are generally depicted as younger girls in uniforms. Their male counterpart is .

They raise a variety of Pokémon.

In Generation I, this class is called Jr. Trainer♀ (Japanese: ガールスカウト Girl Scout, shortened to ガール Girl). The Japanese name was presumably changed in later games for legal reasons, although the class's name remains unchanged in the Virtual Console releases of the Generation I games.

In Let's Go, Pikachu! and Let's Go, Eevee!, Picnickers battled outside of Gyms will award two Great Balls along with prize money upon being defeated.

==In animation==
 
In Pokémon Scent-sation!, multiple Picnickers were working at the Celadon Gym.
 

==In the manga==
===Pokémon Adventures===
 

==== ====
In Gligar Glide, mentioned having met a Picnicker and expecting her to call him back.

==== ====
In I Dare Ya, Altaria... Knock Chic off My Shoulder!, rescued a Picnicker named Kylee (Japanese: ミキコ Mikiko) and her Zigzagoon from a tree. This Trainer is based on a Picnicker of the same name in the Fortree Gym in .

===Pokémon Battle Frontier===
A Picnicker appeared in Enta Arrives at the Battle Frontier!.

==In the TCG==
 
 
Picnicker was introduced as a in the Pokémon Trading Card Game during the English Scarlet & Violet Series (the Japanese Scarlet & Violet Era). It was first released in all four decks of the Japanese Deck Kit. In English, it is included as a included in products such as the and the Deck Kits. This card has the player flip a coin and draw 4 cards from their deck if it comes up heads, or 2 cards if it comes up tails.
 

==Trivia==
In Pokémon GO, "Picnicker" is the name of an achievement awarded for using Lure Modules to help other Trainers catch at least five Pokémon.
